name: TTT Lambda-z Point Selection
description: BioEQ-generated: 3 synthetic single-arm profiles with different Tmax values, confirming the BioEQ TTT (2x-Tmax) lambda_z point-selection rule independently selects the correct terminal window - including the primary rule, the <3-point fallback rule, and a wide (6-point) window proving no truncation.
citation: BioEQ-generated synthetic dataset - internal algorithm consistency check, not benchmarked against external software.

name: Missing Data Handling - Exclude (complete)
description: BioEQ-generated: derived from the bear/WinNonlin Subject 1/Period 1 profile with a BLQ point and two blanked points (one middle, one terminal). Verifies handle_missing_data() with middle_method="complete"/terminal_method="complete" (the app's default) excludes both gaps and always converts BLQ to 0.
citation: BioEQ-generated synthetic dataset - internal algorithm consistency check, not benchmarked against external software.

name: Missing Data Handling - Interpolate
description: BioEQ-generated: same profile as missing_data_complete. Verifies handle_missing_data() with middle_method="interpolate" linearly interpolates the middle gap, while the terminal gap is still excluded (interpolation never applies to terminal points).
citation: BioEQ-generated synthetic dataset - internal algorithm consistency check, not benchmarked against external software.

name: Missing Data Handling - LOCF
description: BioEQ-generated: same profile as missing_data_complete. Verifies handle_missing_data() with middle_method="locf"/terminal_method="locf" carries the last observation forward for both the middle and terminal gaps.
citation: BioEQ-generated synthetic dataset - internal algorithm consistency check, not benchmarked against external software.

name: Carryover Detection (ICH M13A)
description: BioEQ-generated: 3 synthetic 2-period crossover subjects sharing an identical Period-2 Cmax, with pre-dose concentrations at 0.2%, 8.0%, and exactly 5.0% of that Cmax. Verifies detect_carryover() correctly applies the ICH M13A 5% threshold, including the > vs >= boundary case.
citation: BioEQ-generated synthetic dataset - internal algorithm consistency check, not benchmarked against external software.

name: NCA Validation - Theoph (WinNonlin, linear AUC + ARS)
description: All 12 subjects of the base-R Theoph dataset, validating BioEQ's ARS (adjusted-R2 best-fit) lambda_z selection and linear-trapezoidal AUC against published Phoenix WinNonlin 6.3/7.0 output (Bae 2018 / NonCompart-tests). Point counts selected by ARS vary across subjects (3,4,3,3,4,7,4,6,3,3,3,3), demonstrating a genuine search rather than a fixed window.
citation: Bae KS (2018). Development of R packages 'NonCompart' and 'ncar' for noncompartmental analysis (NCA). Transl Clin Pharmacol 26(1):10-15. DOI 10.12793/tcp.2018.26.1.10.

name: NCA Validation - Theoph (WinNonlin, lin-up/log-down AUC)
description: Same 12 Theoph subjects and same WinNonlin reference, isolating the AUC-method-sensitive parameters (AUC0t, AUC0inf, AUC_percent_extrap) under BioEQ's linear-up/log-down ("mixed") AUC method - the app's default.
citation: Bae KS (2018). Development of R packages 'NonCompart' and 'ncar' for noncompartmental analysis (NCA). Transl Clin Pharmacol 26(1):10-15. DOI 10.12793/tcp.2018.26.1.10.

name: NCA AUC Integration Edge Cases
description: BioEQ-generated: 3 short profiles (design taken from PKNCA's own v23-auc-integration-methods vignette) exercising lin-up/log-down's special rules - a Clast-below-LLOQ truncation and zero concentrations mid-profile forcing the linear fallback. All expected AUC0t values are independently re-derived segment-by-segment from the closed-form trapezoid/log formulas, not by calling PKNCA.
citation: BioEQ-generated synthetic dataset (profile shapes from PKNCA vignette v23-auc-integration-methods); internal algorithm consistency check, not benchmarked against external software.

name: NCA ARS Tie-Break (WinNonlin bear reference)
description: BioEQ-generated: reuses the nca_pending profile (bear/WinNonlin Subj T-01) under ARS instead of WinNonlin's manual 3-point selection. This profile's 3-point and 4-point adjusted-R2 fits differ by only 6.9e-06, inside PKNCA's default 1e-4 tolerance, making it a targeted regression test of the best-fit tie-break ("more points wins") rule. Expected values independently computed via lm(log(conc)~time), not by calling PKNCA.
citation: BioEQ-generated synthetic check reusing the nca_pending profile; internal algorithm consistency check, not benchmarked against external software.
